stories.headline: Breaking Free from Shame: The Church's Role in Eating Disorder Recovery
stories.summary: Eating disorders thrive on shame, but a deeper understanding of God's love can set people free. The church can play a vital role in supporting those struggling with these conditions.

stories.headline: Astrology App Rejection Exposes Developer's Hypocrisy
stories.summary: A developer's surprise at his astrology app's rejection from the App Store has backfired, revealing his own double standards. His previous work and disdain for astrology were starkly at odds with his feigned outrage.

stories.headline: Human vs. AI: Tracing Text Edits with Diff-Based Provenance
stories.summary: A new tool uses diff-based line-level provenance to track changes made to text under agentic editing, highlighting the differences between human and AI-generated content. This innovation has significant implications for content creation and verification.

stories.headline: Goth's Rebellious Spirit: The Unapologetic Remix Collection
stories.summary: A club-friendly remix collection serves as a defiant rebuke to critics who sought to constrain goth's musical identity. This spirited rebuke showcases the genre's unapologetic spirit and creative diversity.

stories.headline: Israel Rejects Trump's Gaza Plan, Citing Hamas Disarmament
stories.summary: Israel's Prime Minister has rejected a 15-point plan for Gaza, citing the need for Hamas to be genuinely disarmed before a military withdrawal. This decision underscores the complex challenges facing peace negotiations in the region.

stories.headline: Birth Control Backlash Linked to Rise in Abortions
stories.summary: A growing number of online critics are targeting birth control, potentially contributing to a rise in abortions. Experts are exploring the connection between these two trends and the impact on reproductive health.

stories.headline: Middle East Tensions Escalate Amid Yemen Attack and Iran Demands
stories.summary: Tensions in the Middle East have intensified following a claimed attack on an Aramco oil facility and new demands from Iran regarding negotiations and the Strait of Hormuz. The situation remains volatile and uncertain.

stories.headline: Hormuz Talks Yield Hope, But Breakthrough Remains Elusive
stories.summary: Talks between Iran and Oman have yielded positive signals, but a breakthrough in negotiations to establish a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz remains unclear. Both sides are cautiously optimistic about progress.

stories.headline: Russian Missile Attacks Claim Lives in Ukraine, Including a Child
stories.summary: Russia's continued missile attacks on Ukraine have resulted in the deaths of three people, including a child. The attacks come as Ukraine's supplies of missile interceptors dwindle, raising concerns about the country's defense capabilities.

stories.headline: Claude Code's Auto Mode Becomes Default Setting for Pro Plans
stories.summary: Anthropic has made auto mode the default setting for new sessions in most Claude Code plans, citing confidence in the feature's capabilities. This change aims to streamline the content creation process for users.

stories.headline: Trump's Iran Endgame Eludes Him
stories.summary: President Trump is struggling to find a way out of the prolonged Iran conflict, a challenge that has stumped many of his predecessors. The war's duration is reshaping Trump's presidency and testing his leadership.

stories.headline: Accenture Seeks to Rein in AI Token Abuse
stories.summary: Consulting giant Accenture is trying to prevent non-technical employees from misusing AI tokens for trivial tasks, according to leaked audio recordings. The company aims to ensure its clients' AI investments are used efficiently.

stories.headline: Canada Wildfire Spreads Out of Control
stories.summary: The Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia has spread over 39 square miles, prompting warnings for residents to prepare for the worst. The fire remains uncontained, posing a significant threat to the area.

stories.headline: Ex-Minister Charged in Ecuador Presidential Candidate Murder
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Ecuador have charged a former minister and six others, including a cartel leader, with an indirect role in the assassination of presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. The investigation aims to uncover the full extent of the plot.

stories.headline: Tech Industry Misreads Science Fiction, Undermines Democracy
stories.summary: Historian Jill Lepore argues that the tech industry's poor understanding of science fiction is contributing to the erosion of democracy. She claims that bad readers are driving the industry's misguided priorities.

stories.headline: Tanker Sailors Remain in Limbo at Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An agreement over the Strait of Hormuz remains elusive, leaving tanker sailors in a state of uncertainty. The ships are still at risk of danger while transiting the waterway.

stories.headline: Ukraine Mourns 'Collector of Souls' Oleksiy Yukov
stories.summary: Oleksiy Yukov, a Ukrainian soldier who spent two decades recovering the bodies of soldiers, including many Russians, was killed during a recovery mission. His death has sparked an outpouring of grief in Ukraine.

stories.headline: Israel Accused of Weaponizing Archaeology in West Bank
stories.summary: Israel is planning large-scale land expropriations in historic Palestinian areas of the West Bank, sparking accusations of using archaeology as a tool for territorial control. The move has raised concerns about the impact on local communities.

stories.headline: US Offers $1 Billion to Colombia's New Right-Wing President
stories.summary: The US has pledged $1 billion in aid to Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, who has vowed to wage an 'all-out war' on narco-terrorism. The move aims to strengthen ties between the two countries.

stories.headline: Works & Wonders: A Collection of Curious Essays
stories.summary: The latest installment of Works & Wonders features a collection of essays that explore the intersection of faith and everyday life. The essays offer insights into the human experience and the search for meaning.

stories.headline: US Aims to Block Foreign Drones Equipped with Military-Grade Lidar Technology
stories.summary: The FCC has proposed a ban on Lidar-equipped foreign drones entering the US, citing national security concerns. The move could also impact thermal models and drone light shows.

stories.headline: Criminal Deception Rampant in Silicon Valley
stories.summary: A new study reveals widespread deception and manipulation in Silicon Valley, with companies and individuals engaging in unethical behavior to gain an advantage. The findings raise questions about the ethics of the tech industry.

stories.headline: Drone Sighting Raises Security Concerns at German Military Base
stories.summary: A drone was spotted over a German military base, sparking concerns about potential security breaches. The base is used for housing parts of the Patriot missile system.

stories.headline: Puerto Rico Faces Water Rationing Amid Intense Drought
stories.summary: A severe drought has led to water rationing in Puerto Rico, affecting hundreds of thousands of people. The hot weather and aging infrastructure have exacerbated the crisis.

stories.headline: The Importance of Stable Web Addresses
stories.summary: A 1998 article highlights the importance of using stable and consistent web addresses, which can improve user experience and reduce technical issues. This principle remains relevant today.

stories.headline: Mathematicians Make Progress on HRT Counterexample
stories.summary: Researchers have made a breakthrough in understanding the HRT counterexample, a complex mathematical concept. The findings could have significant implications for the field of mathematics.

stories.headline: French Government Scrambles to Assign Blame for Devastating Wildfires
stories.summary: The French government is under pressure to assign blame for the recent wildfires that ravaged the country. Hundreds of people have been arrested, but the investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: RISC-V Takes Center Stage in Retro Computing Project
stories.summary: A developer has successfully ported the Oberon System to run on RISC-V, a modern processor architecture. The project showcases the versatility of RISC-V.

stories.headline: Kashmir's First India Test Cricketer Makes History
stories.summary: Auqib Nabi has become the first cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir to be selected for the Indian national team. His achievement has inspired millions of people in the region.

stories.headline: Corruption Runs Deep in FIFA's Inner Circle
stories.summary: A group of FIFA officials were caught engaging in suspicious behavior just before the World Cup final, highlighting the deep-seated corruption within the organization. The incident has sparked outrage and calls for reform.

stories.headline: Windows 11 Weather App Guzzles Over 1 GB RAM
stories.summary: Testing shows the built‑in Weather app on Windows 11 can consume more than a gigabyte of memory, even when idle. The bloated usage raises concerns about the OS’s resource efficiency for everyday utilities.

stories.headline: Interactive Globe Maps Cities onto Past and Future Tectonic Plates
stories.summary: A web project visualizes modern urban locations on a reconstruction of ancient plate positions and projected future shifts. Users can explore how continents and cities will move over millions of years.

stories.headline: 1978 John C. Lilly Predicts Solid‑State Minds and Human Obsolescence
stories.summary: Lilly’s archived essay speculates that future computers built from solid‑state materials could surpass human cognition and render humanity redundant. The piece reflects early cyber‑philosophical anxieties about artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Australia’s Biodiversity Crisis Finds a Ray of Hope in One Species
stories.summary: Australia leads the world in recent extinctions, threatening its unique fauna. Conservationists point to a resilient native animal that may help restore ecological balance.

stories.headline: Airy Launches Free, Lightning‑Fast Voice‑First Publishing Tool
stories.summary: Airy is a web service that lets creators record, edit, and publish audio content with minimal friction. The platform emphasizes speed, simplicity, and zero cost for users.

stories.headline: MCP Interceptor Blocks .env Leaks and Hazardous Commands in Real Time
stories.summary: The MarketNow tool monitors processes to prevent applications from exposing environment files or executing risky shell commands. It acts as a safeguard for developers concerned about credential leakage.

stories.headline: Upcoming Solar Eclipse Set to Darken Parts of the U.S. Next Wednesday
stories.summary: A total solar eclipse will be visible across a narrow corridor of the United States on Wednesday. Experts advise safe viewing practices and outline the timing for different regions.

stories.headline: Speedy Writes Shift Load Elsewhere, Not Away
stories.summary: A recent analysis explains that accelerating write operations merely relocates the bottleneck to other system components. The insight challenges the notion that faster storage alone solves performance issues.

stories.headline: Gravity‑Powered Trebuchet Smashes Sound Barrier
stories.summary: Engineer Tom Stanton built a trebuchet that launches a projectile fast enough to exceed Mach 1 using only gravitational energy. The experiment demonstrates extreme kinetic potential without explosives.

stories.headline: Alpha 21264: The 1998 RISC Powerhouse Behind NT
stories.summary: A retrospective looks at the Alpha 21264 processor, which delivered unprecedented performance for Windows NT in the late 1990s. Its architecture set benchmarks that influenced later CPU designs.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Mass Wedding Scheme Struggles to Separate Love from Scams
stories.summary: A Nigerian government initiative aims to help low-income couples marry without financial burdens, but distinguishing genuine love from scams has proven a significant challenge. The scheme's success relies on identifying trustworthy partners.

stories.headline: Open-Source Microsoft Word Ported to 64-Bit Windows
stories.summary: A developer has successfully ported Microsoft Word to 64-bit Windows, making the classic software compatible with modern operating systems. The open-source project is now available on GitHub for users to download and use.

stories.headline: Ancient Roman Shipwreck Uncovered off Sicily's Coast
stories.summary: Italian archaeologists have discovered a significant underwater archaeological find, an ancient Roman shipwreck, off the coast of Sicily. The shipwreck is considered one of the most important finds in recent years.

stories.headline: Solo Sailor Embarks on Record-Breaking Arctic Circumnavigation
stories.summary: Matt Rutherford is attempting to become the first person to sail solo around the Arctic Ocean, navigating treacherous ice floes and gales along the way. He aims to complete the 10,000-nautical-mile journey in a remarkable feat of endurance.

stories.headline: Woman and Infant Killed in Boat Capsizing Near Statue of Liberty
stories.summary: A tragic accident occurred when a boat capsized near the Statue of Liberty, resulting in the deaths of a woman and her infant. Twelve people were rescued by a nearby vessel before police arrived.

stories.headline: Dark Hours: A Cautionary Tale of AI's Limitations
stories.summary: A blog post highlights the limitations of AI, using the example of a fictional AI system that fails to prevent a catastrophic event. The story serves as a reminder of the importance of human oversight and responsibility in AI development.

stories.headline: Mathematicians Discover Magic Hexagons of Every Order
stories.summary: Researchers have made a groundbreaking discovery in mathematics, finding that magic hexagons exist in every order. This finding has significant implications for the field of geometry and number theory.

stories.headline: Banksy's Artwork Comes at a Steep Price for the Public
stories.summary: Banksy's street art has become highly sought after, but the cost to the public is substantial, with some pieces selling for nearly £150,000. The value of his artwork has made it inaccessible to many who appreciate his work.

stories.headline: Cameroonian Artist Brings Renaissance Themes to His Homeland
stories.summary: Marc Padeu's paintings reimagine Renaissance art in the context of a cocoa plantation in Cameroon, blending traditional themes with local culture. His work is currently featured in a gallery show in London.

stories.headline: Taxi Drivers' Complex Mental Maps May Protect Against Alzheimer's
stories.summary: Research suggests that taxi drivers, who rely on complex mental maps and spatial reasoning, may be less likely to develop Alzheimer's disease. This finding has implications for our understanding of the relationship between cognitive function and brain health.
